review_notes: I read the whole file. I paid most attention to the OrderDual section, which holds all the `@[simp]` lemmas. Those are 16 comp-ofDual/toDual iff lemmas for Monotone, Antitone, StrictMono, StrictAnti and their `On` variants, plus `isStable_toDual_comp_iff`. They all rewrite toward the undualised property, so they terminate and give a consistent normal form. The `_dual_iff` lemmas (`monotone_dual_iff` and the rest) are deliberately not simp. The `toDual ∘ (f ∘ ofDual)` form should already be reduced by two applications of the simp-tagged lemmas, so tagging them would add nothing. The conditional rewrites (`StrictMono.le_iff_le`, `lt_iff_lt`, `eq_iff_eq` and similar) are not simp. Mathlib call sites pass them explicitly, for example `simp [hf.lt_iff_lt]`, and they take a hypothesis `hf` that simp could not discharge generically. I found no competing rules, no cycles and no wrongly oriented simp lemmas. The one remaining uncertainty is whether simp's unifier matches the lambda form `fun x => f (ofDual x)` against the `f ∘ ofDual` pattern. I could not check that without running Lean, and I found no use that depends on it.
